newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil Tiger rebels attack Sri Lanka military bases.
newsitem.headline: Tamil Tiger rebels attack Sri Lanka military bases.

text.p: Tamil Tiger guerrillas struck back at Sri Lankan forces on Thursday with pre-dawn attacks on two military bases in the island's east, ending a lull during which the military easily took over large rebel-held areas.

The guerrillas overran a small army camp in the eastern Batticaloa district early on Thursday and attacked an air force base in Trincomalee district badly damaging a transport plane, military officials said.

The attacks came after Sri Lankan troops last month captured a key highway linking two army-controlled towns in the north of the island, with little opposition from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels who controlled large swathes of land south and southwest of the road.

A military spokesman said one air force man was killed and four wounded and a Chinese-made Y12 transport plane damaged when LTTE guerrillas attacked the China Bay air force base in eastern Trincomalee, some 240 km (150 miles) from the capital Colombo.
"The aircraft was heavily damaged. Four air force men were wounded," the spokesman told Reuters. Earlier reports said four air force men were killed.
Police in Trincomalee said about 300 LTTE rebels attacked the China Bay base with mortars and rocket launchers late on Wednesday.

Military officials said casualty figures in the attack on Vaunathivu camp in Batticaloa district, some 200 km (125 miles) from Colombo, were not immediately available but said they were expected to be high.
"The camp was overrun. The situation is not good," said an army official. "Reinforcements have been rushed to the scene."
Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte told parliament on Thursday that the attack on Vaunathivu camp was still continuing.
The military spokesman said there were many LTTE casualties in the China Bay attack, which began at about 11.30 p.m. (1730 GMT) and lasted three hours.
"Two terrorist suicide bombers were killed and a large number of them wounded," the spokesman said.
Another military official said the rebels withdrew after the military launched ground and air attacks.
The spokesman said rebel communications monitored by the army indicated that the LTTE were seeking urgent medical assistance for the wounded.
An LTTE spokesman in London was not immediately available for comment.
The Tigers are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese island's north and east.
Last year, the LTTE overran a key army base on the northeast coast, killing or capturing the camp's 1,000 men and dealing the the military its worst blow in the 13-year war.
In January, the rebels again attacked a military base at Paranthan, a key road junction south of Jaffna. The army said 223 soldiers were killed and the rebels said they lost at least 140.

But the military faced little resistence from the LTTE when troops, backed by artillery, tanks and air cover, advanced in a westerly direction from northern Vavuniya to link up with troops in Mannar last month as part of its latest offensive code-named "Edi Bala" (brave force).
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, but the LTTE says the number is higher.
